newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO reject CIA-Israel bid to restore security ties.
newsitem.headline: PLO reject CIA-Israel bid to restore security ties.

text.p: Palestinian security chiefs refused to restore security ties with Israel in a secret meeting attended by President Yasser Arafat and Israeli and U.S. intelligence officials, PLO officials said on Wednesday.

The officials, who insisted on anonymity, said Arafat was asked by CIA and Israeli security officials in the meeting held in Gaza on Tuesday to restore security cooperation with Israel to prevent further Israeli-Palestinian violence.

"The PLO security chiefs in the West Bank and Gaza Strip who attended the meeting refused to restore security cooperation until political contacts at all levels, including peace talks, were resumed by Israel," the official said.

Israel said after a suicide bomber killed three Israelis at a Tel Aviv cafe last month that it would condition continuation of political talks on a Palestinian crackdown on militants and the strengthening of security cooperation against "terror".
The PLO said security and political talks went hand in hand and that it would halt security contacts with Israel until political talks were restored.

Israeli-PLO peace moves ground to a halt last month after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, touching off street battles between stone-throwing Palestinians and Israeli troops.
Palestinians demand Israel halt work on the East Jerusalem settlement.
A PLO official said during Tuesday's meeting that Arafat insisted he was fighting "terrorism" and containing street protests.

Violence flared again on Wednesday, one day after three Palestinians were killed in the West Bank town of Hebron in the heaviest bloodshed since the crisis began with the East Jerusalem groundbreaking on March 18.
